features: App/browser caches and system temporary files (Linux ~/.cache and /tmp; Windows %TMP% and profile temps)
Application and system logs (including Windows Defender logs in practice)

ui_model: GUI: left-side tree of cleaners with nested options, per-option descriptions/warnings, Preview (list every file/size) then Delete with confirmation; Expert mode (5.1+) locks high-risk options (passwords, empty-space wipe, deep scan, shellbags, etc.) until enabled; cookie manager for selective cookie keep; shred files/folders from menu; preferences for overwrite-on-clean, drives for free-space wipe, languages, allowlist, custom paths. CLI: bleachbit / bleachbit_console.exe with --list-cleaners, --preview, --clean, option wildcards (app.*), --preset, --all-but-warning, --except, --overwrite, --shred, --wipe-empty-space for scripts/cron/Task Scheduler. Extensible CleanerML and optional winapp2.ini. Not a one-click smart-scan wizard; user-driven checkbox selection.
risks: No undo: deletions permanent; overwrite and wipe empty space make recovery unlikely (ZDNET: create restore point first)
Aggressive options: browser passwords, cookies (logouts), sessions, DNF autoremove package removal
Wipe empty space fills the disk for minutes/hours; interrupting leaves huge random files in ~/.cache, /tmp, or %TMP%
Deep scan can flag wanted backups, node_modules, or project files if preview is skipped
SSD free-space wipe is weak (wear leveling) and causes write wear; less useful with full-disk encryption
Admin/root vs user split: system cleaners need elevation; dual runs may be required on Linux
Cleaning while apps (browsers) are open can fail or corrupt profiles
Antivirus false positives on BleachBit installers/binaries due to shredding heuristics
Political brand association (Clinton email server used BleachBit) and early 'Linux registry cleaner' controversy
Historical Recycle Bin junction/symlink following could delete unintended data (called fixed as important in 6.0)
Official product has no ads/upsell/telemetry beyond optional update check; freemium competitors are the upsell contrast
lessons: Default to dry-run/preview with explicit path listing and sizes before any delete
Ship a safe default profile; gate passwords, free-space wipe, and deep scan behind expert mode
Use declarative path rules with XDG/AppData variables; support Flatpak/snap profile layouts
Split reclaim-space, privacy-erase, and secure-wipe into distinct modes with different defaults
Document honest secure-delete limits (1-pass HDD; weak on SSD; prefer encryption)
First-class CLI: list, dry-run, clean, except, presets for automation and library embedding
Refuse to clean if target process is running; support allowlists and custom path include/exclude
Never follow junctions/symlinks into unexpected trees without an explicit policy

Crash-safe wipe: recoverable temp naming and a documented recovery cleaner
No ads, telemetry, or bundled crapware: primary trust differentiator vs freemium cleaners
Do not claim malware removal without a real scanner; do not oversell unrecoverability beyond OS/storage reality
monetization_hooks: BleachBit itself: none (GPLv3, no ads, no upsells, optional update check only)
Freemium cleaners typically upsell: expanded app cleaner packs
Real-time junk monitors and scheduled automatic cleanup
Registry cleaners / startup managers / driver updaters
Bundled antivirus or 'PC health' suites
Paid multi-pass shredding marketed as DoD/Gutmann (often oversold)
Tech-support / remote-help subscriptions
Cloud backup or premium support tiers

features: System Cleaner categories: package caches, crash reports, application logs, application caches, trash
Package cache scan/delete: /var/cache/apt/archives/ (APT) and /var/cache/pacman/pkg/ (pacman)
Crash reports under /var/crash (files)
Application logs: top-level files only in /var/log (not subdirectories)
Application caches: entries under ~/.cache (files and directories)
Empty Trash: ~/.local/share/Trash/files and ~/.local/share/Trash/info
Dashboard: CPU, memory, disk, network rates, basic system info
Startup Apps manager (autostart entries, often ~/.config/autostart)
Services: search, start/stop, enable/disable system services
Processes: list/sort by PID/CPU/memory, end process, refresh rate
Uninstaller for installed packages (dpkg/apt) and Snap packages (later versions)
Resources graphs (~60s) for CPU cores, RAM, disk, load average, network; disk pie chart in later UI
APT Repository Manager: enable/disable/edit/delete package sources
File Search (beta): files, directories, symlinks with advanced options
Helpers: hosts file manager; limited GNOME Settings tweaks; resource threshold alerts
ui_model: Qt desktop GUI with left-sidebar sections (all-in-one optimizer, not a CLI). System Cleaner flow: enable category checkboxes (or select all) -> System Scan -> tree of results with name and size (items unchecked by default) -> check files/categories -> Clean. Privileged actions use sudo; selected non-trash paths are removed with sudo rm -rf; trash is wiped recursively under the user Trash directory. Also includes monitoring, process/service control, uninstaller, APT sources, search, hosts, and GNOME tweaks.
risks: Upstream abandoned: GitHub warns no further releases, so bugs and breakage accumulate
App-cache deletes from ~/.cache can slow app launches and disrupt sessions (e.g. browser re-login)
Deleting application logs can remove useful or important files; docs warn to keep current X.org, Apt, and Dpkg logs
Cleaner uses aggressive sudo rm -rf on selected paths with no documented dry-run, quarantine, or undo
Uninstaller can list and remove core packages; reviews note weak confirmation and no undo
Service toggles can break the session or require a reboot if critical services are stopped
Historical privilege UX: wrong sudo password could still open the UI while actions fail silently
Coarse categories (especially whole ~/.cache and top-level /var/log files) invite over-deletion via select-all
Not a malware or privacy product; optimizer framing can overstate safety/security value
Reports of hangs/slow scans on large cache trees on some distros
lessons: Copy scan-then-select with sizes and default-unchecked results rather than silent one-click mass delete
Copy multi-package-manager awareness for real cache roots (apt archives, pacman pkg cache, etc.)
Copy open-source no-adware model; optional donations instead of nags or bundled upsells
Avoid treating all of ~/.cache as equally safe; split high-risk trees (browsers) with strong warnings
Default-protect critical logs (apt/dpkg/Xorg-class) instead of offering them as ordinary junk
Prefer library+CLI with dry-run, explicit path rules, and clear failure when privileges are missing
Prefer quarantine/trash or --force over immediate irreversible rm -rf as the only path
Stay maintained; an abandoned system cleaner becomes a liability in distro repos
Do not bundle process kill, service disable, hosts edits, or GNOME tweaks into a junk cleaner without hard gates
Require confirmation and safety lists for package removal; never market core packages as casual cleanup
monetization_hooks: Stacer itself: free MIT with Patreon/OpenCollective donations only (no freemium paywall found)
Class comparison (not Stacer): freemium cleaners often upsell scheduled/auto clean, premium monitors, driver updaters, malware add-ons, and multi-device licenses

product: Junk cleaners (Wise Disk Cleaner, Glary Utilities, CCleaner, BleachBit, CleanMyMac)

Recycle Bin / Recent Documents / Quick Access style traces (Wise, PortableApps, Glary Tracks Eraser)

Secure delete / overwrite and free-space or empty-space wipe (Wise Safe Deletion, CCleaner MFT wipe, BleachBit shred/wipe-empty-space)
HDD defrag + SSD TRIM (Wise Disk Cleaner)
Duplicates, large/old files, disk space analyzer, startup manager, software updater (Glary suite; CleanMyMac clutter tools)
Mac system junk, complete app uninstall leftovers, malware scan, cloud cleanup, Smart Care multi-routine (CleanMyMac)

ui_model: Dominant pattern is scan-then-select-then-delete: category trees with Recommended presets (Wise Common Cleaner; CCleaner Analyze/Clean; BleachBit option checkboxes + preview). Suites add a One-Click/Smart/Health wizard (Glary 1-Click Maintenance, CleanMyMac Smart Care, CCleaner Health Check) plus deep modules. Power path is CLI: BleachBit --list-cleaners/--preview/--clean/--preset/--all-but-warning/--except for scripts and scheduled tasks. Safety UX includes ignore/exclusion lists, open file location, export results, and explicit warnings on passwords/cookies (Wise, BleachBit).
risks: Registry cleaners: Microsoft unsupported; can delete needed keys and break apps/OS with little speed benefit
False confidence from huge freeable-space claims and scareware-style problem counts (CCleaner nags; MacKeeper PUP/affiliate fake scans)
Aggressive or irreversible deletes: passwords, cookies, System Restore points, OS help/IME/slimming (Wise SFC warning)
CCleaner 2017 supply-chain malware in official build (~2.27M machines); later breach attempt; trust damage for all cleaners
Telemetry and hard-to-disable monitoring (CCleaner Active Monitoring/Smart Cleaning controversy)
Bundled AV/browser/PUA installers (CCleaner/Avast; Microsoft PUA flag for bundling)
Unwanted persistence: tray apps, scheduled tasks, freemium nags, hard-to-exit startup (CCleaner v7 complaints)
System Slimming / deep OS cleanup that later fails integrity checks or removes needed input methods
Secure wipe misused as performance tool: slow, does not free extra space when wiping empty space
Suite bloat increases attack surface and confuses safe junk vs security claims
lessons: Default to dry-run/preview and Recommended soft targets only; require explicit opt-in for privacy and OS-slimming categories
Ship first-class CLI + library API like BleachBit (list, preview, clean, except, warning flags) for automation without a GUI
Use declarative community-extensible cleaner rules (CleanerML/winapp2-style) instead of opaque binary scanners
Per-path exclude lists, open-location, and exportable scan reports build trust and recoverability
Do not make registry cleaning a core feature; treat Microsoft’s non-support as a product constraint
Never use fake threat counts, inflated freeable GB, or forced AV/browser bundles
Mark irreversible categories (passwords, cookies, restore points, system components) with hard warnings
Prefer offline, no-telemetry operation; any metrics must be opt-in and documented
Separate junk cleaning from malware claims unless real detection is in scope and independently validated
Document OS paths by platform (Windows Temp/Update/browser profiles; macOS ~/Library/Caches and System Data caveats; Linux ~/.cache and package caches)
If automation ships, schedule only the same safe preset as the default GUI—never silent deep wipe
monetization_hooks: Free basic clean → paid suite (Wise Care 365, Glary Pro all-in-one)
Gate scheduler, deep clean, and auto privacy-on-shutdown behind Pro (Glary, CCleaner)
Subscription Mac maintenance (CleanMyMac trial → monthly/yearly)
Cross-sell antivirus, VPN, Chromium browser, driver updater (CCleaner/Gen Digital ecosystem)
Upsell file recovery, shredder, duplicate finder, priority support
Restrict Free to home use; charge commercial/network licenses (CCleaner)
Scareware/PUP affiliate installs (anti-pattern: MacKeeper-class ads—avoid entirely)

risks: Docker --volumes / volume prune can destroy DB and app state when containers are stopped
docker system prune -a removes unused tagged images, forcing re-pulls
Desktop Docker prune may not free host disk until VHDX/Docker.raw compact or Clean/Purge data
Deleting Archives or Device Support loses release history and forces large redownloads
Basename-only targets can hit wrong trees (Unity Library vs ~/Library; generic out/deps)
delete-all / clean-all without dry-run breaks system apps that ship node_modules
Size mis-estimates and non-undoable deletes; cleaning while Xcode/Docker busy causes odd failures
Industry freemium cleaners associated with upsell, telemetry, and past malware scandals—avoid that trust model
lessons: Rebuildable-only catalogs with ecosystem profiles beat vague 'junk' claims
Never auto-select items; interactive consent is the DevCleaner/npkill trust pattern
Separate inventory (df/report) from mutate (prune/delete) like Docker
Warn and gate high-impact classes: volumes, archives, device support, global package stores
Expose dry-run, JSON, and a library API for CI and custom UIs
Show size and staleness so users delete old projects first
Limit default scope to user Home/workspaces; opt-in broader roots
Use path-context rules, not basename-only matching
Stay open, tip/donation optional, no malware/optimizer paywalls or opaque telemetry
monetization_hooks: Optional tips/donations while core CLI stays free (DevCleaner/npkill pattern)
Paid GUI, scheduled reminders, or multi-machine reports without locking scan/delete
Avoid freemium 'scan free / clean paid' and malware-upsell suites used by general cleaners
